ci_support_linux_64_.yaml:
channel_sources:
- conda-forge
channel_targets:
- conda-forge main
docker_image:
- quay.io/condaforge/linux-anvil-x86_64:alma10
python_min:
- '3.11'

about.description:
FastMDXplora runs a complete molecular dynamics study from a single
command. Given a protein structure, or just a PDB identifier, it performs
setup, simulation, analysis, and reporting, and returns publication-ready
results.

Setup repairs and solvates the structure. Simulation runs molecular
dynamics with OpenMM, including optional PLUMED enhanced sampling.
Analysis computes the standard structural and dynamic metrics, along with
protein-ligand measures when a ligand is present. Reporting packages the
results into a written report, a slide deck, and a shareable bundle. A
graphical interface is included for designing, starting, watching, and
reviewing a run.
about.summary: Software for Automated Molecular Dynamics Exploration

script: python -c "from openff.toolkit.utils.toolkits import AmberToolsToolkitWrapper as T; assert T.is_available(), 'no AmberTools, so no ligand charges'"

name: fastmdxplora
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  name: fastmdxplora
  version: "2.5.7"

package:
  name: ${{ name|lower }}
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/${{ name[0] }}/${{ name }}/${{ name }}-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: e0f505152d9bbb45f6d6966504aadc6a7b7e84b110859d5b7f55ac018715b94e

build:
  noarch: python
  number: 0
  script: ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
  python:
    entry_points:
      - fastmdx = fastmdxplora.cli.main:main
      - fastmdxplora = fastmdxplora.cli.main:main

requirements:
  host:
    - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    - pip
    - setuptools >=64
    - setuptools-scm >=8
  run:
    # Upper bound matches requires-python in pyproject.toml; the chemistry
    # stack has no 3.14 builds yet either.
    - python >=${{ python_min }},<3.14
    - numpy >=2.0
    - pyyaml >=6.0
    - mdtraj >=1.9.7
    - matplotlib-base >=3.5
    - scipy >=1.7
    - scikit-learn >=1.0
    - pandas >=1.4
    - python-pptx >=0.6.21
    - pillow >=10.0
    # fastmdxplora accepts AMBER NetCDF trajectories. mdtraj can read them
    # through scipy, but warns that this path is significantly slower and
    # declares netcdf4 in its own metadata; conda-forge's mdtraj does not
    # install it. Including it here gives the fast reader by default.
    - netcdf4
    # The setup and simulation phases need these, and they are only packaged
    # for conda. Depending on them here is the point of the conda-forge
    # distribution: one install command makes all four phases work, where the
    # PyPI package covers analysis and reporting alone.
    - openmm >=8.2
    - pdbfixer
    # Protein-ligand systems need small-molecule parameterization, and the
    # chemistry a structure omits has to be read and its protonation settled
    # in the complex. On PyPI these are the [ligand] extra; here they belong
    # in the package, because one install command is the point.
    - openff-toolkit >=0.16
    # Every ligand takes AM1-BCC charges, and the toolkit computes them by
    # calling AmberTools' sqm. openff-toolkit no longer brings AmberTools, so
    # without this a ligand fails after its system has been solvated.
    - ambertools
    - openmmforcefields >=0.12
    - rdkit >=2023.3
    - propka >=3.5
    # The report as a PDF as well as Markdown. On PyPI these are the [pdf]
    # extra, because WeasyPrint there needs Pango and Cairo installed
    # separately; the conda-forge package brings its own, so a conda install
    # gives the format with nothing further to do.
    - weasyprint >=60
    - markdown >=3.4
    # Enhanced sampling: metadynamics, umbrella sampling, steered MD. Not on
    # PyPI at all, so this is the only distribution that can carry it, and a
    # metadynamics run without it fails at the point of use.
    - openmm-plumed >=1.0

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - fastmdxplora
        - fastmdxplora.setup
        - fastmdxplora.simulation
        - fastmdxplora.analysis
        - fastmdxplora.report
        - fastmdxplora.gui
        # If these fail the recipe has not delivered what it promises.
        - openmm
        - pdbfixer
        # Declaring the small-molecule stack is not the same as it resolving.
        # Importing it here means a broken solve fails the build rather than
        # the first protein-ligand run a user attempts.
        - openff.toolkit
        - openmmforcefields
        - rdkit
        - propka
      python_version:
        - ${{ python_min }}.*
        - "*"
      # Disabled deliberately. AmberTools, a run dependency above, installs
      # Python components (ndfes, edgembar, fetkutils) whose metadata
      # declares numpy<2 while the environment provides numpy 2.x. Nothing
      # in this package imports them, and pinning numpy<2 to satisfy
      # metadata we do not use would be worse than not running the check.
      # The import tests above already prove the stack resolves.
      pip_check: false
  - script:
      - fastmdx --version
      - fastmdx info
      - fastmdxplora --version
      # AmberTools has no module to import, and the toolkit loads without
      # it, so the import tests cannot see it missing. This is what the
      # toolkit asks before it will compute a ligand's AM1-BCC charges.
      - python -c "from openff.toolkit.utils.toolkits import AmberToolsToolkitWrapper as T; assert T.is_available(), 'no AmberTools, so no ligand charges'"
    requirements:
      run:
        - python ${{ python_min }}.*

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/aai-research-lab/FastMDXplora
  summary: Software for Automated Molecular Dynamics Exploration
  description: |
    FastMDXplora runs a complete molecular dynamics study from a single
    command. Given a protein structure, or just a PDB identifier, it performs
    setup, simulation, analysis, and reporting, and returns publication-ready
    results.

    Setup repairs and solvates the structure. Simulation runs molecular
    dynamics with OpenMM, including optional PLUMED enhanced sampling.
    Analysis computes the standard structural and dynamic metrics, along with
    protein-ligand measures when a ligand is present. Reporting packages the
    results into a written report, a slide deck, and a shareable bundle. A
    graphical interface is included for designing, starting, watching, and
    reviewing a run.
  # The package bundles a minified build of 3Dmol.js (BSD-3-Clause) for the
  # molecular viewer in the graphical interface, so its licenses ship too.
  license: MIT AND BSD-3-Clause
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
    - src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/3Dmol-LICENSE.txt
    - src/fastmdxplora/gui/static/3Dmol-min.js.LICENSE.txt
  documentation: https://fastmdxplora.readthedocs.io
  repository: https://github.com/aai-research-lab/FastMDXplora

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - ainaadekunle
